findings: W019 (W081 transition): The draft transition to W081 says 'W216 distributes character across zones; W081 compresses two competing faces into a single dense form.' W216 precedes W081 in the draft, which is correct, but the transition language is accurate and supported by visible evidence — retained.

W009 observation correction: The draft says 'a single grey eye' — the larger anchor image confirms one visible eye with a sideways glance; the other is obscured by the head turn. Observation is accurate.
W019 reading claims 'teeth bared' — the image shows a creature with an open mouth and visible teeth; this is supported. The 'snarl or grin' ambiguity is a legitimate visible reading. Retained.
W036: The observations describe 'square-spiral eye shapes outlined in blue and red' — confirmed visible in image. Gold loops and cross-hatching confirmed. Accurate.
W049: 'pink-magenta outline language' shared between small figure and coiled mass — confirmed visible. Accurate.
W065: 'small masked face' with 'red angular marks and a spiral, topped by two thin antennae' — confirmed visible in image. Accurate.
W081: 'secondary face with bared teeth sits low between the figure's forelimbs' — confirmed visible. The two glowing spiral eyes are confirmed. Accurate.
W091: The draft describes 'a yellow bird perches on a horizontal black line at upper left, beside a small yellow structure; a small dark cat sits at lower left corner' — confirmed visible. Accurate.
W116: 'orange-red goggle-like circles' and 'pale yellow haze' — confirmed. The 'smaller open-mouthed form at lower left' is confirmed visible. Accurate.
W119: The black lobed form on acid-green with orange spiral eyes and zigzag radiating lines — confirmed. The stem and leaf silhouette confirmed. Accurate.
W131: 'small creature perches — its body cyan-blue, wings pink, beak yellow, with an X mark on its head' — confirmed visible. The stretched figure and grey double-frame confirmed. Accurate.
W137: The draft describes a 'single black circle at the bottom' — confirmed visible as a sphere. The arched pose and spiral eyes confirmed. Accurate.
W140: The draft describes 'gold-ringed eyes built from stacked zigzag lines' — confirmed visible. The white dashes on the torso and scattered magenta/teal lines confirmed. Accurate.
W141: 'pale blue pooling shapes sit beneath the hooves' — confirmed visible as blue pooled areas. The looping lines on torso and white zigzag on neck confirmed. Accurate.

W164 (anchor image reviewed): The large teal-grey rounded form with yellow spiral eyes confirmed. The flanking dark rectangular forms with white crown zigzags and crossed-box symbols confirmed. The coiled black spring lines on the right edge confirmed. The blue flower cluster upper right confirmed. The description 'jagged yellow mouth line across its lower edge' is accurate — the mouth is a yellow jagged line. Accurate.

W172: The draft describes 'feather-like forms spread from both sides of the figure's upper body' — the image shows splayed forms spreading from the shoulders that read as feathered or wing-like. The tooth-filled mouth and red-streaked eye sockets confirmed. Accurate.

W194: 'X-marked eyes' confirmed. The 'yellow-orange looping body below' and 'magenta scribble marks form a loose rectangular border' confirmed. The 'small starred burst near the bottom center' — a small starburst mark is visible near the lower center. Accurate.
W197: The toy-like rounded figure on flat yellow confirmed. Spiral eye rings and surface scribbles confirmed. Accurate.
W211: Dense black scribble lines, flame bursts at head and tail, large round eyes with blue-white highlights confirmed. The coiled form lower left confirmed. Accurate.
W216: Three zones confirmed — snail lower left, face-grid upper left, dotted ring upper right. The red branching lines below the ring confirmed. Accurate.
W231: White grid on black cat body, magenta vertical stripe, flower shape over one eye socket, wave band at lower third — all confirmed visible. Accurate.

W235: The image shows two upright forms on a pink background against which the description of 'blocky upright forms layered with competing vertical color streaks' is confirmed. The 'paired red oval marks near a rounded upper mass' are visible on the right form. The gray shadows beneath each form confirmed. Accurate.
W241: The amber/near-black split confirmed. Teeth bared and eye half-lidded confirmed. Layered colored marks on mane confirmed. Accurate.
W252: Two black masses on sky-blue confirmed. The smaller form's yellow rectangular marks and stitched-looking mouth confirmed. Zigzag lines around both forms confirmed. Accurate.
W271: Horizontal banding wrapping the figure confirmed. Two black disc lenses and wide grin with packed teeth confirmed. Flat amber-yellow background confirmed. Accurate.
W293: Pink upright form on black, spiked crest, long toothed snout, thick black wavy neck line, concentric-circle eye — all confirmed visible. Accurate.

W295 (anchor image reviewed): The dark olive-green upright figure is confirmed as a cat-like form. The red crossed lines over the eye areas are confirmed — they are dense red X-cross marks layered over the face. The thin circular outline around the head is confirmed. The pink-blue looped collar at the neck is confirmed. The background is busy with tan/cream washes, orange-yellow blocks, teal strokes, spirals, and red-orange shapes — confirmed. The observation 'yellow outlines trace the feet and a rectangular patch on the lower torso' — yellow outlines at the feet are visible; a rectangular patch on the lower torso is less clearly distinct but yellow outlines are present in that area. Observation is broadly accurate.

W241→W019 transition says 'W211's split is light versus dark; W019's split is cool body against hot ground' — the preceding work is W241 not W211; the transition text correctly references W241's split. Accurate. W019→W140 transition says 'W019's creature moves through its field; W140's head is static but pressed so close to the edge' — supported. W140→W131 transition says 'W140 is dense and close; W131 is spare and stretched' — supported. One prose issue: W019 reading contains 'the collector links this kind of pull between opposites to the emotional range found across the owned subset' — this is an unsupported claim about collector psychology and must be removed from the reading. The whyHere and transition text for W019 do not contain this language, but the reading field is not visitor prose in the gallery output. No action needed in gallery output as readings are not included in the gallery JSON.
W172 description says 'feather-like forms spread from both sides' — image shows splayed radiating forms from shoulders that could be wings or feathers; the description is cautious enough. Retained.

W235: The description mentions 'A smaller fragmented cluster in the upper left includes a rectangular frame, a wedge of white zigzag lines' — looking at the image, the upper left area does contain a rectangular frame-like structure and zigzag elements. Confirmed broadly accurate.

Minor language issue: W081 whyHere says 'the dense hatched body makes both hard to hold at once' — this is a legitimate perceptual observation about competing focal points, not an unsupported claim. Retained.

W271 observation says 'a row of small, tightly packed white shapes rendered with scratchy overlapping lines; a dark curved outline frames them above and below, but no large open cavity is clearly visible' — the image confirms a wide grin with packed teeth but the mouth is not wide open. Accurate.
No slots are missing or duplicated. All 26 slots appear exactly once across the five chapters.

title: Characters Beyond the Human Face
question: What makes a shape read as a character?
introduction: Animal-like silhouettes, unusual bodies and less clearly defined forms offer different paths toward recognizing a character. Look at eye shapes, mouth marks and stance before settling on a name. Some contours support a familiar reading; others leave it uncertain. Compare the details that establish a character with the marks that make its boundaries harder to follow.
closing: Return to a form whose identity remains uncertain. Can you describe the visible shapes that suggest a character without deciding exactly what it is?

chapters.title: Silhouette and Signal
chapters.introduction: Four figures whose outlines read immediately as animal or creature, each using a different minimum set of marks to confirm that reading.

stops.whyHere: A flat yellow beak and single visible eye are the minimum signals needed; dense layered strokes do the rest of the character work.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #56

stops.whyHere: Where nnxyz nnotb #56 uses layered colour to build volume, here a flat black silhouette on acid-green does the same job with almost nothing — two orange spirals and a jagged mouth suffice.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: From dense painterly marks to pure flat silhouette: both figures read instantly, but by opposite means.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #122

stops.whyHere: Pink on black, a long toothed snout and spiked crest — the silhouette is unambiguous, yet the thick wavy neck-line fractures the form just enough to introduce doubt.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The flat-on-flat logic continues, but the fractured neck introduces a crack in the clean silhouette that nnxyz nnotb #122 never allowed.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #265

stops.whyHere: Two black masses share a blue field; the smaller one's yellow rectangular eyes and stitched mouth confirm character while the larger form stays mute beside it.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #265 is a single loud pink shape; here two black forms share the frame, and only one carries the face marks — the other remains ambiguous.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #133

chapters.title: Bodies and Posture
chapters.introduction: Figures whose stance — arched, hunched, braced, or crouching — carries as much descriptive weight as any mark on the face.

stops.whyHere: An extreme arched pose balanced on a single sphere; the body's position reads as alarm or display before the spiral eyes confirm it.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Moving from a static silhouette pair to a figure caught mid-action: posture now does the character work the face was doing before.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #53

stops.whyHere: Head dropped, spine arched, legs planted — the burdened stance reads before the warm looping lines across the torso add their own layer of unease.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Both figures arch their spines, but nnxyz nnotb #53 reads as agitation while nnxyz nnotb #284 reads as weight — the same posture carrying opposite charges.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #284

stops.whyHere: Front-facing, wings spread wide, heavy feet planted — a posture of display or threat, with the small masked face arriving late as a stranger detail.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #284 faces sideways with a lowered head; nnxyz nnotb #39 faces directly out, wings thrown open — the shift from private strain to public confrontation.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #39

stops.whyHere: A crouching figure with feathered shoulder forms and a long toothed mouth; the crouch pulls the body inward while the spread lines push outward.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #39 stands upright and wide; nnxyz nnotb #27 folds low and forward, the same outward energy now compressed into a crouch.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #27

stops.whyHere: A small upright figure and an enormous coiled mass share the same outline language; scale difference alone creates the tension between them.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #27 is a single figure whose energy spreads outward; nnxyz nnotb #40 splits that energy between two forms of radically different size.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #40

chapters.title: The Face as Mask
chapters.introduction: Works where the face is drawn as a set of applied marks — spirals, grids, crosses — laid onto a form rather than built into it.

stops.whyHere: Square-spiral eyes and rectangular teeth sit on a black cat mass like a mask laid over a silhouette — the face reads as added, not grown.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #40 uses scale to create unease; nnxyz nnotb #255 uses the gap between a naturalistic silhouette and its mask-like face markings.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #255

stops.whyHere: A black cat form again, but now a white grid covers the body and a flower shape replaces one eye — the figure reads as catalogued or annotated rather than alive.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Both are black cat silhouettes with applied face marks, but nnxyz nnotb #255's marks feel decorative while nnxyz nnotb #246's grid reads as inventory.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #246

stops.whyHere: Red crossed lines over both eyes, a pink-blue collar, a thin circle around the head — adornment and obstruction occupy the same marks simultaneously.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #246's grid covers the whole body; nnxyz nnotb #248 concentrates its applied marks on the face alone, making the crossing-out more pointed.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #248

stops.whyHere: Yellow spiral eyes and a jagged mouth on a large teal form flanked by crown-marked shapes — the face is assembled from signals, the surrounding marks repeating them like an echo.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #248 is a single figure with a busy face; nnxyz nnotb #155 spreads the face-signal logic outward into the whole composition.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #155

stops.whyHere: X-marked eyes and an open mouth on a green face, with a small starred burst below repeating the X motif — the face mark becomes a pattern across the image.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #155's spiral eyes echo in flanking shapes; nnxyz nnotb #2 takes one eye mark and repeats it at a different scale within the same frame.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #2

chapters.title: Softness and Its Limits
chapters.introduction: Figures that approach rounded, toy-like familiarity while other visible marks — scribbled surfaces, sealed grins, goggle lenses — pull against that reading.

stops.whyHere: Balloon-like limbs and a flat yellow surround suggest a toy, but spiral eye rings and surface scribbles sit visibly on top, refusing to let the softness settle.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #2's marks read as alarm; nnxyz nnotb #111 uses similar layered marks on a form that invites comfort — the same technique, a different starting point.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #111

stops.whyHere: A hunched figure assembled from restless layered lines that never close into solid mass; the orange goggle eyes glow inward rather than outward.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #111 is rounded and toy-like; nnxyz nnotb #99 is similarly soft in outline but the body never solidifies — the comfort is less available here.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #99

stops.whyHere: Bands of white and grey wrap a bulbous figure completely; two black disc lenses and a packed-tooth grin read as cheerful and sealed at once.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #99's body is open and semi-transparent; nnxyz nnotb #275's is wrapped tight — both withhold something, but by opposite means.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #275

stops.whyHere: A crowned white figure with loose open lines holds the center while smaller figures — bird, cat, distant form — occupy the edges without competing for its weight.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #275 is a single sealed form; nnxyz nnotb #247 opens the frame to multiple presences, the central figure's looseness contrasting with nnxyz nnotb #275's tight wrapping.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #247

stops.whyHere: Three zones share one field without merging: a face-grid that shifts from expressive to blank, a slow spiral creature, a dotted ring — character distributed rather than centred.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #247 has a clear central figure with peripheral presences; nnxyz nnotb #42 refuses a centre, spreading character signals across three separate zones.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #42

chapters.title: Density and the Edge of Recognition
chapters.introduction: Works where layered marks, competing color fields, or compressed scale push the figure toward the limit of readability, held together by the minimum necessary marks.

stops.whyHere: Two glowing spiral eyes and a hidden secondary toothed face compete for attention; the dense hatched body makes both hard to hold at once.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #42 distributes character across zones; nnxyz nnotb #79 compresses two competing faces into a single dense form.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #79

stops.whyHere: Dense black scribble lines hold a compact form together while flame bursts at head and tail and large reflective eyes pull against the surrounding weight.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #79's two faces create internal competition; nnxyz nnotb #59 has one face but the body's density and the flame bursts create a similar pull between mass and signal.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #59

stops.whyHere: The figure splits sharply between amber glow and near-black; teeth bared, eye half-lidded — the light division does as much character work as the face marks.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #59's density is uniform across the frame; nnxyz nnotb #128 splits the figure in two by light alone, making half the body a shadow that the face must work against.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #128

stops.whyHere: A heavy creature moves left, teeth bared, its body a tangle of cool lines against a hot orange field — the ambiguity between snarl and grin sits at the centre.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #128's split is warm light against deep black; nnxyz nnotb #66's split is cool body against hot ground — figure and field in active competition.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #66

stops.whyHere: A dark animal head pushes close to the picture edge, gold-ringed eyes built from stacked zigzag lines; figure and warm ground compete for the same plane.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #66's creature moves through its field; nnxyz nnotb #243's head is static but pressed so close to the edge that containment itself becomes uncertain.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #243

stops.whyHere: A stretched near-monochrome figure reaches across most of the frame toward a tiny vivid creature; the wide grey space makes the reach feel effortful and the character feel earned.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #243 is dense and close; nnxyz nnotb #129 is spare and stretched — compression and extension as opposite ways of holding a figure in the frame.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #129

stops.whyHere: Two blocky upright forms layered with competing vertical colour streaks; paired red oval marks near a rounded mass invite a face reading that never fully resolves.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #129's figure is unmistakable despite its sparseness; nnxyz nnotb #35 offers the minimum marks for a face reading and then withholds confirmation.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #35
